messages:
jess: Hey folks — I pushed a docs PR that adds a small postinstall cert verification step for private/offline installs and a concise SDK example for calling KMS through a local tunnel. Asking for a quick review of the wording + the netpolicy snippet. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4822 :eyes:

marco: taking a look now. main question: are we documenting the port the KMS agent exposes on the tunnel side? customers keep confusing 8443 vs 7443 in airgap guides.

jess: good call — I added a short note that the default agent binds to 7443 but the installer can remap. I also included a port matrix link to the table in network-ports.md.

sam: quick nit: the link to the port matrix in the new paragraph points to /network/ports.md#matrix which 404s. We moved that page under docs/networking/port-matrix.md last month.

jess: thanks — will update. does anyone have a terse cert chain verification snippet we can include? want something customers can run offline to ensure the bundle was installed correctly.

marco: toss this in (bash):
```bash
# verify cert chain with openssl
openssl s_client -connect localhost:7443 -CAfile /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem -showcerts 
```
Works for most; mention to use -servername for SNI in multi-host setups.

kevin: also add a small systemd-ready script example for the postinstall check so customers can run it automatically after install. Something like:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
if openssl s_client -connect localhost:7443 -CAfile /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem -brief </dev/null 2>&1 | grep -q "Verify return code: 0"; then
  echo "certs OK"
  exit 0
else
  echo "cert verify failed"
  exit 2
fi
```
Link it from the guide and call out exit codes for systemd.

jess: perfect. I'll add both snippets and a systemd unit example. Also included a Python SDK snippet for KMS-over-tunnel that uses requests + client cert:
```python
import requests
resp = requests.post(
  'https://127.0.0.1:7443/v1/sign',
  cert=("/etc/redwood/agent-client.pem", "/etc/redwood/agent-client-key.pem"),
  verify='/etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem',
  json={"payload": "..."}
)
print(resp.json())
```

sam: tiny doc style point: call out that the SDK example assumes the tunnel is bound to loopback and that firewall rules must allow localhost->agent. Also we should recommend explicit iptables/netpolicies for clusters that restrict hostNetwork.

marco: added an example netpolicy for calico to the PR comments:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-agent-local
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: installer
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 7443
```

kevin: heads-up: line 214 in the new markdown has a stray backtick around the config key `agent.tls.bundle` — that breaks the fenced YAML preview in the site generator. Remove the extra backtick.

jess: fixed the backtick and updated the broken port-matrix link Sam found. Also added a short troubleshooting checklist: cert permissions, system time skew, and verifying agent logs (`journalctl -u redwood-agent`).

docs-ci-bot: docs-lint: markdown lint passed with 1 warning (link-title-mismatch). See CI run: https://ci.internal/redwood/docs/4822/checks/16

sam: can we add a one-line migration note for customers who upgraded from the older installer that used 8443? "If you previously used 8443, check agent config map 'agent.port' and migrate TLS bundles to /etc/redwood/" — I can draft if you want.

jess: yes please add that bullet. I'll also squash and rebase per CI. Planning to merge after Kevin and Marco give final ack. :shipit:

marco: ack from me after the netpolicy YAML moves into the examples folder. :+1:

kevin: ack after CI shows zero warnings. small but important improvement — nice work on making the offline verification more actionable. :clap:

jess: thanks all — merging once CI is clean. I'll follow up with a short changelog blurb and update the support playbook with the verify steps.
